name: TOS-1A

placement_rationale.text: TOS-1A's own characteristics state a short ~6–10 km engagement envelope (6 km baseline, up to 10 km with newer extended-range rockets), so the previous 21 km siting placed the launcher entirely outside its own maximum range — it could not have reached the front line from there. Corrected to 6 km, which keeps it within its stated envelope while leaving some margin under the ~10 km extended-range ceiling; this matches doctrine.md §2's FPV strike range (0–10 km), the same zone this asset's own characteristics already flag as making TOS-1A 'a high-value target if located' once it fires from inside it. There is little standoff room to trade away for a system this short-ranged — survivability rests on concealment and infrequent firing rather than distance, an inherent limitation of the platform rather than a siting choice.

characteristics: 24-tube 220mm thermobaric rocket launcher, built on a T-72 chassis, short range (~6-10km class)
Strength: Thermobaric warheads are especially effective against fortified positions and trench networks
Limitation: Very short range compared to standard MLRS, forcing it close to the line where it is a high-value target if located
Estimated quantity available: Fleet size not fully disclosed
employment_notes: Used specifically against dug-in infantry and fortified positions - a direct counter to the trench/fortification-heavy defensive style both sides have adopted
contrast_vs_traditional: Thermobaric rocket fire exists to defeat exactly the passive countermeasures doctrine.md documents infantry adopting against everything else on this battlefield — trench side-niches, "G"-shaped dugout exits, dispersed fighting positions built to survive an FPV or a single artillery round. A short-range weapon built for mass and blast overpressure is one of the few tools that still punches through a fortified position rather than having to pick it apart target by target.
